title: Progress 'rows' field is seeded to 0 and never updated by any producer, so /progress always reports rows=0
description: `_start_build_progress` seeds the per-path progress dict with `"rows": 0` (line 76), and `_get_build_progress` reads it back as `int(current.get("rows", 0))` to populate `JsonCacheProgressResponse.rows` (line 104). However, nothing in the codebase ever writes `_build_progress[key]["rows"]` to a non-zero value — the only mutations to the progress dict are the full-dict initialisation (line 72) and `active_count` increments/decrements (lines 79, 92), and `build_per_port_cache` (the threaded builder) does not touch `_build_progress` at all (it has no reference to the module's progress state). Consequently the `GET /api/json-cache/progress` endpoint's `rows` field is permanently 0 — the same value the schema would default to. The `"rows": 0` seed and the `current.get("rows", 0)` read are vestigial plumbing for a row-count feed that was never wired up, which is mildly misleading to API consumers who may expect a live row count during a long build.
evidence: Grep for `_build_progress` in json_cache.py shows writes only at line 72 (init dict), 79 (`current["active_count"] = ...`), 90/92 (finish), with no `[...]["rows"] = ` assignment. build_per_port_cache (_json_shred.py:748+) returns a summary dict but never imports or mutates routes.json_cache._build_progress. Therefore _get_build_progress:104 `int(current.get("rows", 0))` evaluates to 0 on every poll for every build.
est_reduction: Either remove the `"rows": 0` seed and the `rows=` argument from _get_build_progress (the schema default keeps it 0), or wire a real per-build row counter through _build_progress; today the field is dead.
behavior_preservation: Dropping the seed and the explicit `rows=...` argument is behavior-preserving: JsonCacheProgressResponse.rows already defaults to 0, which is the only value the endpoint can currently emit.
